headline: On last trading day, Sensex slumped over 1,400 points as banking and financial stocks led market sell-off.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Wednesday, 25 November.

why: Heavy profit-taking in banking, metal, and financial stocks halted a four-week rally.
Investor wealth worth over ₹5.6 lakh crore was wiped out in a single session.
The Sensex dropped over 1,400 points while the Nifty slipped below the 25,400 mark.
Selling pressure mounted across major financial sectors despite an initial positive opening.
whatHappening: Indian stock markets are shut today, 24 November 2026, on account of Guru Nanak Jayanti.
US stocks rallied strongly as Nvidia surged 31% following Jensen Huang's reinstatement.
Asian indices such as Nikkei and Kospi jumped up to 8% driven by the global tech rally.
Brent crude oil prices slipped below $89 per barrel due to rising supply from the Middle East.
summary:
Indian share markets are closed today, Tuesday, 24 November 2026, for Guru Nanak Jayanti and will reopen tomorrow.
In the last session, Indian benchmark indices fell sharply by over 1.7% due to profit-taking in financial and metal stocks.
Globally, markets rallied strongly following a massive surge in US tech stocks and lower crude oil prices.
